Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 72, verses 18–28:

{18} ﴿And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah﴾; i.e., no invocation of worship and no invocation of request, for the mosques, which are the greatest places of worship, are founded upon sincerity to Allah, submission to His greatness, and humility before His might.

{19} ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up invoking Him﴾; i.e., calling upon Him, asking Him, worshipping Him, and reciting the Qur'an, the jinn nearly became ﴿on him a mass﴾ because of their crowding around him; i.e., pressing and piling up upon one another, eager to [hear] what he brought of guidance.

{20} ﴿Say﴾: to them, O Messenger, clarifying the reality of what you call to: ﴿Indeed, I only invoke my Lord and associate none with Him﴾; i.e., I single Him out alone, with no partner, and I renounce whatever is other than Him of rivals and idols, and everything the polytheists take besides Him.

{21–22} ﴿Say: Indeed, I do not possess for you any harm or any guidance﴾: for I am a servant who has no share in the affair or in its disposal. ﴿Say: Indeed, none will protect me from Allah, and I will not find besides Him any refuge﴾; i.e., there is no one I could seek protection from to save me from the punishment of Allah. If the Messenger, who is the most complete of creation, does not possess harm or guidance and cannot shield himself from Allah in anything if He intends him with evil, then others among creation are all the more and more fittingly so. ﴿And I will not find besides Him any refuge﴾; i.e., a shelter and a helper.

{23} ﴿Except a notification from Allah and His messages﴾; i.e., I have no distinction over the people except that Allah has singled me out to convey His messages and call His creation to Him, and by this the proof is established against the people. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾: this refers to disobedience that is disbelief, as is specified by the other clear texts. As for mere disobedience, it does not necessitate eternal abiding in the Fire, as the verses of the Qur'an and the hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ) indicate, and the early generations of the Ummah and its imams have agreed upon this.

{24} ﴿Until, when they see what they are promised﴾; i.e., they witness it directly and are certain that it will befall them. ﴿Then they will know﴾ at that time the reality of knowledge ﴿who is weaker in helpers and fewer in numbers﴾: when no one else helps them, nor can they help themselves, and when they are gathered individually, as they were created the first time.

{25–26} ﴿Say﴾ to them, if they ask you, saying: "When is this promise?": ﴿Say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near or whether my Lord will appoint for it a long term﴾; i.e., a lengthy period. The knowledge of that is with Allah, ﴿the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone﴾ from creation; rather, He alone has knowledge of the hidden thoughts, secrets, and unseen matters.

{27} ﴿Except whom He has approved of among messengers﴾; i.e., He informs him of what His wisdom requires that He inform him of. This is because the messengers are not like others: Allah has supported them with a support He gave to no one else among creation, and has preserved what He revealed to them until they convey it in its true form, without the devils approaching it to add to it or subtract from it. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards﴾; i.e., they guard it by the command of Allah.

{28–29} ﴿That He may know﴾ by this ﴿that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾: through the means He placed at their disposal. ﴿And He encompasses what is with them﴾; i.e., what is with them, what they conceal, and what they make public. ﴿And He has enumerated everything in number.﴾

In this surah there are many benefits:
Among them: the existence of the jinn, and that they are accountable, commanded, forbidden, and recompensed for their deeds, as is explicit in this surah and elsewhere.
Among them: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent to the jinn just as he was sent to mankind, for Allah turned a group of jinn toward him to listen to what was revealed to him and to convey it to their people.
Among them: the intelligence of the jinn and their knowledge of the truth, and that what drove them to faith was what they realized of the guidance of the Qur'an and their good manners in addressing Him.
Among them: Allah's care for His Messenger and His preservation of what he brought. When the glad tidings of his prophethood began, the sky was guarded by stars, the devils had fled from their places, and were driven away from their observation posts. And Allah showed mercy through him to the people of the earth with a mercy beyond measure, and their Lord desired guidance for them. He willed to make manifest in the earth from His religion, His law, and His knowledge what hearts rejoice in, what people of understanding delight in, what the symbols of Islam are made apparent by, and by which the people of idols and images are subdued.
Among them: the intense eagerness of the jinn to listen to the Messenger (ﷺ) and their crowding around him.
Among them: that this surah includes the command to monotheism and the prohibition of association with Allah, and it clarifies the condition of creation, that each one of them does not deserve from worship even the weight of an atom; for the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), if he does not possess benefit or harm for anyone, nor even for himself, then it is known that all of creation is likewise. So it is an error and an injustice to take as a god one who has this description.
Among them: that the knowledge of the unseen is solely possessed by Allah; no one among creation knows it except whom Allah approves and singles out with knowledge of some part of it.

The tafsir is complete, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
